roadmap.title: What is built and what is next

blocks.text: Seekprotocol is live on iOS and Android with location-based drops, AR rendering and the social wallet. The verification stack currently runs the GNSS, attestation and motion-continuity signals; radio fingerprinting is in staged rollout. Attestation is enforced behind a flag, which is the honest state of it: the refusal path is built and the enforcement switch has not been thrown for every surface.

The drag-and-drop campaign builder is built. Next is the self-serve business portal that opens placement beyond managed partnerships, and the arrival analytics that go with it. Alongside that sit the token generation event, live event mode, seasons and object scanning. Governance follows once there is enough real fee flow for parameter decisions to be meaningful, for the reasons set out in chapter eleven.
What we are not promising

items: A date for governance. It is gated on volume, and volume is not a date.
Indoor accuracy parity. It is a hard problem and the honest answer is wider radii indoors for the foreseeable future.
A cross-chain deployment. The latency and cost requirements in chapter five are narrow, and a second chain that does not meet them would be a marketing decision rather than a technical one.

blocks.text: The full phase-by-phase breakdown lives on the roadmap page, which is kept current as things ship.
Terms used throughout this document, with the meaning they carry here rather than the one they carry in general.

community.label: Community rewards
community.note: Earned by seekers through collection and quests

proof-of-location.definition: The claim that a device was inside a given radius during a given window, scored across several independent signals and credible enough to release value on. Probabilistic, never absolute.

confidence-score.definition: The combined result of scoring a claim's signals. Each asset sets the score it requires, so a quest reward and a ticketed drop can share a verifier and not share a bar.

claim-radius.definition: The distance from an asset's coordinates within which it can be taken. Default 30 m, configurable from 5 m to 500 m, and the single biggest lever a publisher has over both cost and meaning.

drop.definition: An asset placed at coordinates, waiting to be claimed. Carries a quantity, a window, a confidence threshold and a radius.

spawn.definition: A drop as the game presents it: announced by the server, visible on the map, expiring within the hour, and worth two catch attempts.

attestation.definition: A signed statement from the operating system that the app is genuine and the device untampered. Play Integrity on Android, App Attest on iOS. The strongest signal in the stack and the one the protocol does not control.

radio-fingerprint.definition: The set of Wi-Fi networks and cell towers visible from a position, matched against what should be visible there. Slow to change and hard to fabricate, which is what makes it useful.

motion-continuity.definition: The accelerometer trace between one confirmed position and the next. Catches the claim that teleports, because moving 400 km in 90 seconds leaves no matching motion profile.

verified-arrival.definition: A claim that met its threshold inside a publisher's radius. The unit a publisher buys, and the reason the cost figure on a campaign is counted rather than modelled.

placement-fee.definition: What a publisher pays to hold ground, weighted by radius, duration and demand for the area. Distinct from the reward, which is what the seeker receives.

cold-streak.definition: The pity timer. Two points of catch chance per consecutive miss, capped at twelve, applied to the retry as well as across coins.

streak-penalty.definition: The opposite lever. Four points off per consecutive success on the same coin, capped at twenty, so a single spawn point gets worse to farm rather than better.

seeker.definition: A person who walks to assets and claims them. Also the first of ten player levels, the last being Legend.

seek.definition: The settlement and coordination asset. Funds campaigns, pays placement fees, buys placement priority through staking, and carries the governance vote once governance is live.

whitepaperFigures.donutAria: Token allocation by share of total supply
whitepaperFigures.noMatch: Nothing matches that. The document itself is searchable with your browser's own find.
whitepaperFigures.stackCaption: Claims travel down the stack; value travels back up. Select a layer for detail.
whitepaperFigures.shortBy: Short by {short}. Repeated refusals from one device raise its threshold further.
whitepaperFigures.confidenceCaption: Weights are illustrative. The point is the shape: no signal alone clears a funded campaign, and forging all four at once costs more than the drop.
whitepaperFigures.timelineCaption: These are budgets, not measurements. The sensor window and the settlement both move with conditions, and everything between them is arithmetic that does not. Note where the boundary sits: raw sensor data never leaves the first three stages.
whitepaperFigures.vestingAria: Circulating supply by allocation over 48 months
whitepaperFigures.vestingCaption: Read the steps, not the curve. A flat stretch followed by a jump is a cliff, and a cliff is where a schedule either holds or does not. Team and backer allocations are the ones worth checking, because they are the two that unlock into a market rather than out to the people using the network.
whitepaperFigures.calcFee: Placement fee at this radius: ${fee} per drop
whitepaperFigures.calcInferred: impressions, of which roughly {visits} become an inferred visit at ${cost} each
whitepaperFigures.calcCaption: Display figures use a ${cpm} CPM and a {rate}% impression-to-visit rate, both industry rules of thumb. The difference that matters is that one column is measured at the door and the other is inferred.
whitepaperFigures.ladderTitle: The catch roll, as the server computes it
whitepaperFigures.ladderHint: One spawn tells you almost nothing. Run a thousand and watch the two bars close.
whitepaperFigures.ladderTally: {caught} caught from {spawns} spawns, {gap} points off the model.
whitepaperFigures.ladderCaption: The migration publishes {rarity} at {first}% then {second}%, {overall}% across the spawn. That is this model at level 5 with the ring filled and no clan, which is what the sliders start on. A caught unit is a game unit, and what it is worth in tokens is the market's business rather than the game's.

app.label: Application
app.detail: What people touch. The mobile app renders assets in AR and handles collection; the portal is where publishers place them. Both are ordinary clients of the layers below and hold no privileged access.

intelligence.label: Intelligence
intelligence.detail: Reads the camera feed and your play history to suggest where to go next and what you are looking at. Runs on-device where it can, and never sees raw position history it does not need.

location.label: Location verification
location.detail: Scores a claim across independent signals and emits a signed attestation when the score clears the asset's threshold. Off-chain by design: the sensor data that makes verification work is exactly the data that should not be public.

settlement.label: Settlement
settlement.detail: Holds asset definitions, coordinates and claim records, and moves value when a claim is accepted. A network is configuration rather than an integration, and the bar each one has to clear is fees low enough that collecting a small reward is not dominated by the cost of collecting it.

gnss.label: GNSS fix
gnss.detail: Satellite position and its reported accuracy, plus constellation and satellite count.
gnss.spoofable: Trivially spoofed on a rooted device.

radio.label: Ambient radio
radio.detail: Nearby Wi-Fi SSIDs and cell towers matched against what should be visible here.
radio.spoofable: Hard to fabricate; radio environments change slowly.

attest.label: Device attestation
attest.detail: Play Integrity or App Attest confirming a genuine app on an untampered OS.

motion.label: Motion continuity
motion.detail: The accelerometer trace between your last confirmed position and this one.
motion.spoofable: A 400 km jump in 90 seconds has no matching motion profile.

fund.label: Publisher funds
fund.body: A campaign is denominated and funded in $SEEK, with a placement fee weighted by radius, duration and how contested the area is.

place.label: Asset is placed
place.body: The drop is written to its coordinates with a claim radius, a window, and the confidence threshold it demands.

walk.label: Someone walks there
walk.body: The only step that cannot be automated. Travel is the cost that makes farming expensive.

verify.label: Presence is verified
verify.body: Four signals are scored off-chain. What reaches the chain is a signed attestation, not your sensor data.

settle.label: It settles
settle.body: The transfer confirms in under a second for a fraction of a cent, on the chain the asset lives on, and the claim record is public.

split.label: Fees flow back
split.body: The majority of protocol fees route to the people doing the walking; the rest funds the treasury and the ecosystem.

open.label: Drop opened
open.detail: You tap an asset on the map or reach for it through the camera. The app takes the position it already holds and starts a fresh sensor window.

window.label: Sensor window
window.detail: The longest stage by far, and the one that decides everything after it: a new GNSS fix with its accuracy, a scan of the radio environment, and the motion trace since the last confirmed position.
window.payload: GNSS fix, satellite count, Wi-Fi and cell set, accelerometer trace

attest.label: Attestation and signature
attest.detail: Play Integrity or App Attest confirms the app is genuine and the OS is untampered. The claim is signed by the key bound to that app instance, which is what makes a relayed claim expensive.

score.label: Scoring
score.detail: Off-chain, because it depends on sensor data that has no business being public. Each signal is scored against what the coordinate should look like and the results are combined into one confidence number.

threshold.label: Threshold check
threshold.detail: The score meets the asset's threshold or it does not. A refusal is recorded against the device, and repeated refusals raise the bar for that device rather than only failing again.

settle.label: Settlement
settle.detail: The claim record and the transfer land on the settlement chain in one transaction. This is the only stage anyone else can see, and all it says is that a claim at a public coordinate succeeded.

confirm.label: In your wallet
confirm.detail: The wallet updates and the asset is gone from the map for you. From tapping to holding, under two seconds on a good connection.

referrals.title: Every friend who plays makes you stronger
referrals.lead: Hand a friend your invite code and you keep 5% more XP on every catch you make, for as long as they keep playing. No cap, and it never comes out of their side.
referrals.exampleLabel: One legendary catch, before and after
referrals.exampleBody: The bonus is applied when the catch is scored, on the server, and written into the record alongside your clan rank so the two can be told apart later.
referrals.activeRule: Active means {needed} catches in the last {days} days

once.title: One inviter, chosen once
once.body: A code can be redeemed a single time and never changed after. The database refuses the second attempt, so it is not a rule the app can be talked out of.

newOnly.title: New accounts only
newOnly.body: A code only works on an account with no XP and nothing collected yet. An established seeker cannot attach itself to a team afterwards and be counted as fresh.

oneLevel.title: One level deep
oneLevel.body: You earn from the friends you brought in, not from the friends they bring in. Those seekers build their own team, and keep all of it.

friendKeeps.title: Your friend loses nothing
friendKeeps.body: The bonus is added to your own catches. It is not a cut of theirs, so nothing you gain is taken off anyone.

referralInfo.title: What a team is worth, and when it starts counting
referralInfo.lead: Two things are easy to get wrong here. The bonus has no ceiling, and a friend does not start paying the moment they install. Both are worth seeing rather than being told.
referralInfo.ladderLabel: Active friends, and what your catches are worth
referralInfo.noCap: There is no cap. Twenty active friends is a straight doubling, and nothing in the sum stops there.
referralInfo.lifecycleLabel: How a friend becomes a referral
referralInfo.foot: A friend counts once they have {needed} real catches inside {days} days. Fall short and they stop counting; play again and they are back. Nothing is lost either way.

share.title: You hand over your code
share.body: Every seeker gets an eight character code at signup. It is yours for good and there is nothing to claim or generate.

redeem.title: They enter it on a fresh account
redeem.body: A code only takes on an account with no XP and nothing collected. It is written once and cannot be changed after, so nobody can be moved between teams.

play.title: They go out and play
play.body: Only real catches count. Attempts made in a simulator are recorded separately and are not part of the total.

count.title: They start paying, and keep paying
count.body: This is the step people miss. Installing is not enough: the friend has to actually be out there before your multiplier moves.
